questions.q: What is Cypress's defining architectural choice?
options: Tests run on a cloud grid only
Tests run in a separate Node process driving the browser remotely
Test code runs inside the same browser as the application under test
questions.explain: That gives direct access to the app's window and network layer.

questions.q: Which kinds of tests is Cypress built for?
options: End-to-end tests of web apps (and component tests) written in JavaScript/TypeScript

questions.q: Why do Cypress tests have direct access to the page's window object?
options: Because the test code executes in the same browser context as the app

questions.q: What's a downside of running inside the browser?
options: Constraints like same-origin rules and limited multi-tab support

questions.q: What does `npm install cypress --save-dev` do?
options: Installs Cypress as a dev dependency of the project
questions.explain: The binary is downloaded on install.

questions.q: Where do you set baseUrl and spec patterns?
What does `baseUrl` let you do?
Why verify configuration by running tests rather than trusting defaults?
options: Defaults and docs can differ from actual behavior on your setup
questions.explain: The lesson tests what config actually controls.

questions.q: What does cy.get('.item') do?
options: Queries the DOM for elements matching the selector, retrying until found or timeout

questions.q: How does cy.contains('Login') differ from cy.get?
options: It finds an element by its text content

questions.q: What does `.find()` do?
options: Searches for descendants within the previously yielded subject

questions.q: What does Cypress show when a selector isn't found?
options: A specific timed-out error saying it failed to find the element after retrying
questions.explain: The lesson captures the real message.

questions.q: What does .type('hello') do?
options: Types text into the focused or yielded input

questions.q: What happens when you .click() a disabled button?
options: Cypress fails by default, because it checks actionability

questions.q: What does .check() act on?
Why does Cypress check actionability before clicking?
options: To act like a real user: element must be visible, enabled and not covered

questions.q: What does `cy.get('h1').should('have.text','Todos')` do?
options: Retries until the heading's text matches or timeout

questions.q: When is `expect()` appropriate?
options: On values already extracted, e.g. inside .then()

questions.q: What does `.and()` do?
options: Chains another assertion on the same subject (alias of should)

questions.q: Why can a should with a callback retry?
options: Cypress re-runs the callback until it passes or times out

questions.q: What does automatic retry-ability do for a 1.5s-delayed element?
options: Cypress keeps retrying the query/assertion until it appears (default timeout 4s)

questions.q: Why run the test 10 times in the lesson?
options: To measure real reliability rather than trust one lucky pass

questions.q: What's wrong with `cy.wait(2000)` for an element?
options: Arbitrary sleeps are slow and brittle; assert on the condition instead

questions.q: What's the default command timeout?
Which command picks a dropdown option?
questions.explain: Works with value or visible text.

questions.q: How do you choose a radio option?
What should a login-form test assert after submit?
options: The resulting UI or URL change, such as a welcome message

questions.q: Why prefer data-* attributes for selectors?
options: They're stable and independent of styling and structure

questions.q: What does cy.visit('/page') do?
options: Loads the page and waits for the load event

questions.q: Does text typed into an input survive cy.go('back') then forward?
options: It depends on browser form restoration, so test it rather than assume

questions.q: What does cy.reload() do?
What does cy.location('pathname') yield?
options: The current URL path for assertion

questions.q: What is `cypress run`?
questions.explain: cypress open is the interactive runner.

questions.q: Which browser does Cypress use by default in run mode?
What does `cypress info` show?
Why run in headless mode on CI?
options: No display is needed and it's scriptable and faster
questions.explain: Videos and screenshots can still be saved.

questions.q: What makes the login-flow project good practice?
options: Zero manual waits and assertions that retry

questions.q: How should invalid login be tested?
options: Assert the specific error message appears

questions.q: Where should test data live?
options: In fixtures or config, not hard-coded across tests

questions.q: What makes each test independent?
options: It sets up its own state and doesn't rely on previous tests

questions.q: What does Cypress.Commands.add('login', ...) create?
options: A reusable custom command callable as cy.login()

questions.q: What did renaming the login button's id show?
options: With a custom command only one place needs fixing instead of every test

questions.q: Where are custom commands usually defined?
When is a custom command a bad idea?
options: When it hides assertions or becomes a grab-bag; keep them focused

questions.q: What does cy.fixture('users') do?
How do you drive the same flow with several data rows?
options: Loop over fixture rows and generate tests/iterations

questions.q: What's a benefit of JSON fixtures?
Can fixtures also stub network responses?
What does cy.intercept() do?
options: Spies on or stubs network requests

questions.q: What's the difference between spying and stubbing?
options: Spying observes real requests; stubbing returns a fake response

questions.q: Why stub a server error response?
options: To test the UI's error handling deterministically

questions.q: How do you wait for an intercepted request to complete?
questions.explain: Wait on the route, not time.

questions.q: What does cy.request() do?
options: Makes an HTTP request directly from Cypress, bypassing the browser UI

questions.q: What happens on a 401 from cy.request by default?
options: The command fails unless failOnStatusCode is false

questions.q: Why log in via cy.request?
options: Faster and more reliable than UI login for setup

questions.q: Why seed data via API?
options: Quick known state without clicking through the UI

questions.q: Why can't cy.get see inside an iframe by default?
options: The iframe has a separate document; cy.get queries the top document

questions.q: What's the usual workaround?
options: Access iframe.contentDocument body and wrap it, or use a plugin

questions.q: What does the course say about the iframe limitation?
options: It's reported honestly as a real limitation

questions.q: Cross-origin iframes add what difficulty?
options: Same-origin policy blocks access to their DOM

questions.q: How do you upload a file in Cypress?
Where do upload fixtures live?
What should you assert after upload?
options: The UI shows the file name or success message

questions.q: What does selectFile's drag-drop action do?
options: Simulates dropping the file onto a drop zone

questions.q: How do you read an environment variable in a test?
questions.explain: Set via config, env file or CLI.

questions.q: How do you pass env vars on the command line?
Why keep secrets out of cypress.config.js committed files?
options: They'd leak in source control; use CI secrets

questions.q: What's baseUrl per environment used for?
options: Pointing the same tests at staging or local

questions.q: Which hook runs before each test?
What belongs in beforeEach?
options: Setup that gives each test a fresh known state

questions.q: Why avoid relying on test order?
options: Tests should be independent and runnable alone

questions.q: What does `afterEach` risk?
options: Cleanup may not run if the browser crashes; prefer cleaning in setup

questions.q: What does cy.pause() or .debug() help with?
options: Stopping the run to inspect state

questions.q: What does the Command Log show?
options: Each command and its snapshot you can time-travel through

questions.q: How do you see a failing test's page state in CI?
options: Screenshots and videos saved on failure

questions.q: What's a good first step for a failing selector?
options: Check the DOM snapshot at that step to see what exists

questions.q: What does the network-stubbed suite achieve?
options: Fast deterministic tests independent of the backend

questions.q: What should still be tested without stubs?
options: A few real end-to-end flows to catch integration issues

questions.q: What does asserting on the request body check?
options: That the UI sends the right payload

questions.q: What risk comes from heavily stubbed tests?
options: Stubs can drift from the real API, hiding breakage

questions.q: How does Cypress execute commands?
options: Queues them and runs asynchronously in order; commands don't return values directly

questions.q: Why does `const el = cy.get('x')` not give an element?
options: cy commands return chainables, not elements; use .then() or aliases

questions.q: When does the queued command actually run?
options: After the test function finishes enqueueing, in order

questions.q: Why does mixing plain JS async/await with cy commands cause trouble?
options: Cypress commands aren't promises and don't work with await

questions.q: What does .as('todos') do?
options: Creates an alias for later reference

questions.q: How do you reference an element alias?
Why use aliases for intercepts?
options: To wait on and assert about specific requests

questions.q: What does `this.alias` require?
options: Using function() rather than an arrow function and a context

questions.q: What does retry-ability retry?
options: Queries and assertions, not actions like click

questions.q: Why is `cy.get('x').click().should('...')` risky?
options: Click isn't retried, so a re-render between can break the chain

questions.q: What causes detached DOM errors?
options: Element re-rendered between query and action

questions.q: How do you make assertions robust?
options: Assert on the stable end state, not intermediate steps

questions.q: What does cy.session() do?
options: Caches and restores login state (cookies/localStorage) across tests

questions.q: What does cy.clearCookies() do?
Why log in once per spec via session?
options: Saves time versus UI login before every test

questions.q: How do you set a cookie?
What can cy.intercept's routeHandler do?
options: Modify request or response, delay or fail it

questions.q: How do you simulate a slow network?
options: Use delay in a stub or throttle the response

questions.q: How do you assert a request body?
What happens with overlapping intercept routes?
options: Handlers run in reverse definition order until one responds

questions.q: When are screenshots taken automatically?
Where are videos useful?
options: Diagnosing CI failures you can't watch live

questions.q: What does cy.screenshot() do?
options: Captures the page or an element on demand

questions.q: Why keep artifacts as CI outputs?
options: Developers can inspect failures after the run

questions.q: What's a first step in diagnosing a flaky test?
options: Run it many times and look at the failure pattern

questions.q: Common causes of flakiness include...
options: Race conditions, shared state and unstable selectors

questions.q: What does Cypress's test retries feature do?
options: Reruns failing tests up to N times

questions.q: Why not just add cy.wait(ms)?
options: It slows tests and masks the real race

questions.q: What does `cypress run --browser chrome` do?
options: Runs the suite headlessly in Chrome

questions.q: Why cache node_modules and the Cypress binary in CI?
What should CI start before tests?
options: The app under test, and wait until it's ready

questions.q: What should fail the CI job?
What does parallelization do?
options: Splits specs across machines to shorten total time

questions.q: What balances parallel runs?
options: Spec duration history when using the cloud service

questions.q: What's a requirement for parallelizing specs?
What's an alternative to the cloud for splitting?
options: Manually shard spec lists across CI jobs

questions.q: What is the Page Object Model?
options: Encapsulating page selectors and actions in classes/modules

questions.q: What does POM improve?
options: Maintenance: UI changes touch one place

questions.q: What should page objects avoid?
options: Embedding assertions that hide test intent

questions.q: Cypress's own guidance on page objects?
options: They're optional; custom commands and app actions may be simpler

questions.q: Why is Cypress's architecture different from Selenium's?
options: Tests run in the browser rather than controlling it over a remote protocol

questions.q: What advantage follows from running in the browser?
options: Fast, reliable access to DOM, network and app state

questions.q: What trade-off follows?
options: Language support is JS/TS and some browser limitations apply

questions.q: What is the architecture's effect on flakiness?
options: Fewer timing issues because Cypress knows the app's state and retries

questions.q: What is Cypress component testing?
options: Mounting individual components in a real browser and testing them in isolation

questions.q: When choose component tests over e2e?
options: For fast, isolated checks of UI logic

questions.q: What does cy.mount() require?
options: A framework adapter (React, Vue, Angular, etc.)

questions.q: What do component tests not cover?
What does cy.origin() enable?
options: Running commands against a second origin in one test

questions.q: When do you need it?
options: When the test navigates to a different superdomain (e.g. SSO)

questions.q: What's a constraint of cy.origin callbacks?
options: Variables must be passed explicitly, they don't capture outer scope

questions.q: Why was multi-origin once impossible?
options: Cypress enforced a single superdomain per test

questions.q: What is the same-origin constraint?
options: Within a test Cypress couldn't visit different superdomains without cy.origin

questions.q: Why does it exist?
options: Cypress runs inside the browser and must obey its security model

questions.q: How do you avoid it for login?
options: Log in via cy.request or session instead of UI at the third party

questions.q: What does the lesson say about honesty?
options: These constraints are real and should be understood

questions.q: What does cy.task() do?
options: Runs Node.js code in the Cypress process (e.g. DB seeding)

questions.q: Why can't tests access the filesystem directly?
options: They run in the browser; use cy.readFile or cy.task

questions.q: Where are plugins/tasks configured?
What must a cy.task handler return?
How should you measure test run time fairly?
options: Repeat runs and compare distributions, noting caching and machine differences

questions.q: What typically dominates Cypress test time?
options: Page loads and UI interactions, not command overhead
questions.explain: Reduce UI steps via API setup.

questions.q: How can you speed suites up?
options: API-based setup, session caching and parallelization

questions.q: Why not optimize without measuring?
options: You may speed up the wrong thing

questions.q: A big difference of Cypress vs Selenium?
options: Cypress runs in-browser with auto-waiting; Selenium drives browsers via WebDriver and supports more languages and browsers

questions.q: When might Selenium be the better choice?
options: Broad browser/language support or testing non-web contexts

questions.q: What's easier in Cypress?
options: Debugging with time-travel snapshots and auto-retry

questions.q: What is a Selenium Grid analogue?
options: Cypress Cloud parallelization or CI sharding

questions.q: A difference between Cypress and Playwright?
options: Playwright controls browsers out of process with multi-tab/browser support; Cypress runs inside the browser

questions.q: Which supports multiple browser engines natively?
Which has built-in parallelism without a paid service?
options: Playwright runs workers in parallel by default
questions.explain: Cypress parallelization via Cloud or manual sharding.

questions.q: Why compare tools honestly?
Which is a Cypress antipattern?
options: cy.wait(5000) instead of asserting on a condition

questions.q: Why avoid tests depending on each other?
options: They fail unpredictably when run alone or reordered

questions.q: Why avoid conditional testing (if element exists)?
options: The DOM can change after the check so it's flaky; make state deterministic

questions.q: Why not use brittle selectors like nth-child chains?
options: They break on layout changes; use data-* attributes

questions.q: What does the capstone combine?
options: Custom commands, fixtures, intercepts, sessions, CI and reports

questions.q: What makes a framework maintainable?
options: Clear structure, stable selectors, reusable commands and independent tests

questions.q: How do you prove the framework is reliable?
options: Run repeatedly in CI and track flake rates

questions.q: What should be documented?
options: How to run, add tests and interpret failures

questions.q: A Cypress test types into an input after the page loads and the field renders 1.5 s late. What's the right approach?
options: Rely on automatic retry: cy.get(...).type(...) with no manual wait
questions.explain: Queries retry until the element exists or the timeout hits.

questions.q: Why does `const btn = cy.get('button'); btn.click()` not behave like normal JavaScript?
options: cy commands enqueue and return chainables, not elements; the DOM query hasn't run yet

questions.q: Which part of `cy.get('.row').should('have.length', 3)` is retried?
options: The query and the assertion together until they pass or time out

questions.q: A test does `cy.get('.btn').click().should('be.visible')` and fails with a detached element after a re-render. What's the fix?
options: Re-query after the action and assert on a stable end state

questions.q: Which is the best selector for a Save button?
A test depends on a todo created by the previous test. What's wrong?
options: Tests must be independent; create state in beforeEach or via API
questions.explain: Order dependence is a flakiness source.

questions.q: Login via the UI before each of 50 tests is slow. What do you do?
options: Use cy.session() or cy.request to authenticate quickly, and test the login UI once
questions.explain: Separate setup from what you test.

questions.q: You want to test the UI's error state when the API returns 500. What do you use?
How do you wait for an API call before asserting on the UI it updates?
Why does `cy.request()` returning 401 fail the test by default?
options: failOnStatusCode is true; set it false to assert on error responses

questions.q: A test needs to read a file and seed a database. Which Cypress feature runs Node code?
questions.explain: Tasks run in Node via setupNodeEvents.

questions.q: The test visits your app, clicks 'Login with SSO' and lands on another domain. What do you need?
options: cy.origin() for commands against the other origin

questions.q: Content inside an iframe isn't found by cy.get. Why?
options: The iframe has a separate document; get the iframe's body and wrap it
questions.explain: A real limitation, solved with a helper command.

questions.q: A test fails only in CI. What's the most useful evidence?
options: Screenshots, video and the command log from the failed run

questions.q: Your suite has 30 specs taking 40 minutes. How do you speed it up safely?
options: Shard or parallelize independent specs and move setup to API calls

questions.q: A flaky test passes after Cypress test retries. What should you still do?
options: Track it as flaky and fix the root cause

questions.q: When would you choose Playwright or Selenium over Cypress?
options: Multi-tab or multi-browser needs (e.g. WebKit) or non-JS languages

questions.q: Which is an antipattern?
options: Using `cy.wait(5000)` to wait for an element

questions.q: Component tests vs e2e: which fits checking a form component's validation messages quickly?
options: A component test mounting the component in isolation
questions.explain: Fast and isolated; keep a few e2e flows too.

challenges.title: Model retry-ability
challenges.prompt: Implement retry(check, {timeout, interval}) using a fake clock: call check(elapsed) repeatedly, advancing elapsed by `interval`, until check returns {ok:true} (return {passed:true, elapsed}) or the next step would exceed `timeout` (return {passed:false, elapsed, error}). Use it to compare an element that appears after 1.5 s and one after 6 s.
challenges.explain: Cypress doesn't sleep for a fixed time: it re-runs the query and assertions until they pass or the 4 s default timeout expires, so the delayed element passes at 1500 ms and the 6 s one fails with the last error. This is a model of that behavior, not Cypress code. Verified by running the solution in Node.

challenges.title: Model the command queue
challenges.prompt: Complete the tiny command queue: each command should enqueue a function and return `cy` so calls chain, and nothing runs until runQueue(). Observe that the test body's own log line runs before any enqueued command, just like in Cypress.
challenges.expected:
queued: 4
test body finished | visit /login | get #user | click | then callback
challenges.explain: Cypress commands are enqueued while your test function runs and executed afterwards in order, which is why plain JS around them runs first and why you can't assign a command's result to a variable. This is a teaching model of the idea, not Cypress internals. Verified by running the solution in Node.
